source: LLMAO: Yang et al. (2024) Large Language Models for Test-Free Fault Localization (ICSE 24)
finding: Fine-tuned bidirectional adapters on 350M, 6B, 16B code LLMs find buggy lines with no coverage or tests. Beats learned (ML) FL baselines. Skill grows with model size.
numbers: Top-1 up 2.3%-54.4% and Top-5 up 14.4%-35.6% over ML FL baselines. Defects4J-trained; paper notes SBFL depends on test suite coverage and pass/fail counts.
limits: Needs fine-tuning on small bug corpora; compared to ML baselines, not directly to a fresh Ochiai run in the abstract.
agent_relevance: Shows coverage is not required for line-level FL. Our agent has no tests in some tasks, so a non-spectrum fallback exists.

source: Xiao et al. (2026) Large Language Models for Fault Localization: An Empirical Study
finding: Four LLMs (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4.1 mini, Gemini-2.5-Flash) on statement-level FL, HumanEval-Java and Defects4J, source-code-only input vs PMD and LineDef.
numbers: Prompt styles tested: zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought. Bug report context improved FL on Defects4J. Few-shot: gains only in some cases. CoT: mixed by model.
limits: Abstract and intro read; no coverage spectrum used in this study. Exact tables not recorded.
agent_relevance: Warns that CoT and few-shot are not reliable boosters for localisation; do not assume more prompt scaffolding helps.

source: Ji et al. (2024) Impact of Large Language Models of Code on Fault Localization
finding: Fine-tuned LLMs of code with a sequence-generation framing to name faulty lines without a coverage matrix or compilable code.
numbers: Abstract states the method removes the need for compilable code, existing tests and per-language coverage tools that learning-based FL needs.
limits: Only abstract and intro read for this line; no per-benchmark figures recorded.
agent_relevance: Same lesson as LLMAO: spectrum inputs are costly to build, LLMs can skip them, at some accuracy risk.

source: Kang, An, Yoo (2024) A Quantitative and Qualitative Evaluation of LLM-Based Explainable Fault Localization (AutoFL)
finding: AutoFL gives the LLM the failing test and function-call tools to browse the repo, then asks for a location plus explanation. Compared to Ochiai/DStar (SBFL) and Metallaxis (MBFL).
numbers: 798 real bugs (Java Defects4J, Python BugsInPy). Method-level acc@1 up 19.7% over Ochiai on Defects4J and 166.7% (GPT-3.5) and 233.3% (GPT-4) on BugsInPy. At acc@3 and acc@5 GPT-3.5 AutoFL lagged SBFL; GPT-4 AutoFL beat all baselines up to acc@5.
limits: SBFL is much worse on BugsInPy (cited from Widyasari et al.). GPT-3.5 struggled to dig deep into the repo.
agent_relevance: Top-1 is where an LLM beats coverage ranking; deeper ranks still favour spectrum lists with a weak model.

source: Kang et al. (2024) AutoFL: repeated runs and cost
finding: Running AutoFL several times and merging results raised accuracy. One GPT-4 run beat five merged GPT-3.5 runs. Confidence from agreement can flag false positives.
numbers: Time per Defects4J bug: 16.4 s for one GPT-3.5 run, 87.24 s total for five runs plus prep and merge. SBFL time cited from Zou et al.: 112 s.
limits: Times depend on 2023 API speed. GPT-4 total per bug was 310 s on Defects4J.
agent_relevance: Self-consistency voting over several localisation runs is a cheap analogue of aggregating spectra. Fits our S5 attempts.

source: Qin et al. (2025) AgentFL: Scaling LLM-based Fault Localization to Project-Level Context
finding: Multi-agent ChatGPT pipeline in three steps: comprehension, navigation, confirmation. Uses test behaviour, failure info and doc-guided search.
numbers: Defects4J-V1.2.0: 157 of 395 bugs at Top-1 (183 Top-3, 187 Top-5). Defects4J-V2.0.0 (226 bugs): 78 Top-1, 119 Top-3, 140 Top-5, versus Ochiai 32, 74, 93 and GRACE 85 Top-1. Cost about $0.074 and 97 s per bug.
limits: GRACE edges AgentFL at Top-1 on V2.0.0 (85 vs 78) per table. Uses ChatGPT, possible training leakage.
agent_relevance: An LLM pipeline with no coverage ranking more than doubles Ochiai at Top-1. Cost is small.

source: Qin et al. (2025) AgentFL ablation
finding: Removing parts of the pipeline lowers Top-1 on 395 bugs.
numbers: Top-1: full 157; without Test Behavior Analysis 148; without Test Failure Analysis 125; without Method Doc Enhancement 133. User study: 98 of 395 bugs had no suspect found and were excluded; 297 pairs used, 15-minute limit.
limits: Test-behaviour step helped least, since the test code already carries most of the information (average 4.93 utility methods per test).
agent_relevance: Failure info matters most. Explaining the failing test is worth more than extra context about passing behaviour.

source: Rafi, Chen (2026) Order Matters: LLM Input Order Bias in Software Fault Localization
finding: LLM FL accuracy depends strongly on where the buggy method sits in the prompt. Reversing order collapses accuracy.
numbers: Top-1 Java falls from 57% to 20%, Python from 38% to about 3% when the order is reversed. Splitting into smaller contexts narrows the gap from 22% and 6% to 1%. Renaming methods did not remove the bias, so not leakage.
limits: Two benchmarks (Java and Python). ICSE 26 version.
agent_relevance: If we feed coverage-ranked lists, rank order is a hidden bias. Put the Ochiai-top first, but chunk contexts to cut position bias.

source: Rafi, Chen (2026) Order Matters: SBFL ordering versus static ordering
finding: Ordering the LLM input by Ochiai (statistical) did not beat simple static orders such as call graph from the failing test.
numbers: CallGraphBFS: 175 bugs Top-1 (34.9%); CallGraphDFS 173 (34.5%); Statistical (Ochiai) ordering 32.7% Top-1. DepGraph (learned) ordering reached 48% Top-1.
limits: Differences among simple orderings are small. Ochiai used at method level.
agent_relevance: Spectrum scores are a weak prior for ordering LLM input. Learned or structural orders can be better.

source: Shi, Yang, Chen (2026) From Finding to Fixing: How Useful is Fault Localization for Agentic Program Repair?
finding: Six recent FL methods plugged into one repair agent, on SWE-bench Verified and Defects4J with three LLMs. FL does not reliably raise repair success.
numbers: 16,248 repair trajectories. Accurate locations cut repair tokens by up to 39.2%, but current FL methods often spend more tokens than they save. Gold bug-cause descriptions help beyond gold locations. Example: GPT-5.6 Luna with AutoFL on Defects4J had No-FL pass@1 of 79.2% for Top-1 hits.
limits: Higher localisation accuracy did not map to larger repair gains. A single reference patch under-counts valid locations.
agent_relevance: Do not over-invest in a separate localisation stage. Agents already find code; cause hints help more than locations.

source: Sepidband, Pham, Hemmati (2026) On the Role of Fault Localization Context for LLM-Based Program Repair
finding: 61 context configurations with GPT-5-mini on 500 SWE-bench Verified instances. File-level localisation dominates; line-level context often hurts.
numbers: File-level localisation gives 15-17x over a no-file baseline. Best repairs seen at about 6-10 relevant files. Line-level expansion frequently degrades results due to noise.
limits: One model (GPT-5-mini), one benchmark.
agent_relevance: Coarse-then-precise localisation. Adding many suspicious lines (a long spectrum list) can add noise.

source: Haroon et al. (2026) Assessing the Impact of Code Changes on the Fault Localizability of LLMs
finding: Large mutation-style test of 10 LLMs on injected faults, then semantics-preserving changes (SPMs). LLM localisation leans on surface form.
numbers: 750,013 FL tasks, over 1300 Java and Python programs. After an SPM, the model fails on a fault it had found before in 78% of cases. Code earlier in context is reasoned about better.
limits: Underspecified programs filtered out. Faults are injected, not natural.
agent_relevance: LLM localisation is brittle. A spectrum score is invariant to renaming; hybrids can use that.

source: Yang et al. (2026) SemLoc: Structured Grounding of Free-Form LLM Reasoning for Fault Localization
finding: LLM writes semantic constraints as runtime checks; the violation counts over passing and failing tests form a spectrum, scored with Ochiai. Counterfactual patch verification.
numbers: 809 real bugs (SemBugs) plus QuixBugs, four LLMs. Where coverage ties the faulty line with at least half of covered lines: 40.9% ranked first vs 2.2% for SBFL and 7.0% for Daikon. 99.4% of constraints compile to checks. 68.4% of top answers carry a test-confirmed patch, of which 93.6% are correct. Direct LLM with same inputs 82.0% vs SemLoc 81.4%; function-only LLM 50.0%.
limits: SemLoc did not beat an LLM given the same inputs (no significant difference). Gains are in verifiability.
agent_relevance: Best direct use of SBFL ideas in an LLM loop: build a spectrum over LLM-proposed checks, not over lines.

source: Yang et al. (2026) SemLoc: how often SBFL fails
finding: Coverage spectrum fails when failing and passing tests run the same lines and only values differ.
numbers: SBFL fails to rank the faulty line first in 83.8% of 809 real bugs. Example: softmax adds max instead of subtracting, all tests cover the same lines. Under coverage collapse Ochiai misses the top five in 55.1% of cases.
limits: Python-heavy dataset with data-value faults. TSSB-3M cited: over three million such one-line fixes.
agent_relevance: Data-value bugs defeat coverage ranking. For our agent, S5 should compare values, not just which lines ran.

source: Rafi et al. (2025) LLM4FL: Multi-Agent Fault Localization via Graph-Based Retrieval and Reflexion
finding: Splits Ochiai-sorted coverage into groups that fit the LLM window, a debugger agent navigates the call graph, a reviewer self-critiques.
numbers: Defects4J V2.0.0, 675 faults, GPT-4o-mini. Top-1: LLM4FL 327; Ochiai 121; DeepFL 257; Grace 298; DepGraph 359; AutoFL 275; SoapFL/AgentFL 311. Top-10: LLM4FL 494, Ochiai 413.
limits: DepGraph (a learned model) still beats it at every N. Not every fault is covered after prioritisation.
agent_relevance: A direct recipe: Ochiai order, chunk, LLM re-rank, self-review.

source: Rafi et al. (2025) LLM4FL ablation
finding: Each component helps. Self-reflection helps without any external oracle.
numbers: Top-1: full 327; without code navigation 273 (-16.51%); without coverage division 251 (-23.24%); without reflexion 290 (-11.31%).
limits: One benchmark and one model.
agent_relevance: Chunking the spectrum and a self-review pass are each worth 10-23% Top-1.

source: Rafi et al. (2025) LLM4FL ordering experiment
finding: Initial method order given to the LLM changes accuracy: Execution order vs Ochiai order vs DepGraph order.
numbers: Top-1 varies by up to 22% between orderings. DepGraph order was best.
limits: Ochiai gives a decent prior but not the best.
agent_relevance: Spectrum rank is a cheap, useful first sort.

source: Xu et al. (2025) FlexFL: Flexible and Effective Fault Localization with Open-Source LLMs
finding: Two stages: reduce the search space with existing FL families (incl. SBFL), then an open-source LLM re-checks method code.
numbers: With Llama3-8B it locates 42 and 63 more bugs than AutoFL and AgentFL (GPT-3.5). Finds 93 bugs at Top-1 that non-LLM FL cannot. Contamination check on a dataset Llama3-8B had not seen.
limits: Defects4J focus; exact table totals not recorded here (abstract read).
agent_relevance: Spectrum as a pre-filter plus LLM verification works even with a small model.

source: Xu et al. (2025) Exploring Potential and Limitations of LLMs for Novice Program Fault Localization
finding: 13 LLMs (6 closed, 7 open) on Codeflaws, Condefects and a new leakage-safe set BugT. Reasoning models need little prompt engineering; non-reasoning ones (GPT-4) need careful prompts.
numbers: o3 and DeepSeek-R1 top accuracy. Accuracy falls as problem difficulty rises. Over-reasoning (long explanations) hurt clarity. Participants with one year experience rated explanations highly.
limits: Student-style programs. Cost remains a barrier. Abstract read.
agent_relevance: Scaffold value depends on model: reasoning models gain little from added prompt structure.

source: Widyasari et al. (2024) Demystifying Faulty Code with LLM: FuseFL
finding: Prompt with SBFL ranking, test results and code description to GPT-3.5, then step-by-step explanation.
numbers: 324 faulty files (Refactory, 1.85 faulty lines each). Top-1: Tarantula 89, Ochiai 117, OP2 115, Barinel 89, DStar 115, XAI4FL 149, FuseFL 197. FuseFL beats Ochiai by 68.4% and XAI4FL by 32.3%. Cohen d 0.30-0.71 vs SBFL at Top-1. 22 of 30 sampled explanations correct.
limits: Small student-style programs. Top-3 gap small (p=0.052 vs Ochiai, OP2, DStar).
agent_relevance: Directly tests spectrum-in-prompt versus spectrum alone.

source: Widyasari et al. (2024) FuseFL prompt ablation
finding: Which inputs help the LLM. Spectrum scores alone are the weakest extra.
numbers: Top-1 by prompt: Baseline 150; CoT 163; TestRes 187; SusScore (SBFL) 169; CodeDesc 180; SusScore+TestRes 192; TestRes+CodeDesc 190; SusScore+CodeDesc 177; all three (FuseFL) 197. SusScore added 3.7% over CoT at Top-1 (text) . Of 77 cases where SBFL missed Top-3, SusScore prompt got only 8 at Top-1.
limits: Test results gave the largest single gain. Single run, GPT-3.5. Table column alignment from PDF text; numbers read from Table IV.
agent_relevance: Failing test output beats the spectrum as an LLM input; spectrum adds a little.

source: Widyasari et al. (2024) FuseFL error types
finding: Runtime errors localise easier than wrong-output errors.
numbers: Among failed localisations, 78.5% were output errors, 21.5% runtime errors. Of 117 faults Ochiai got at Top-1, FuseFL also got 116 (99%). 81 faults found only by FuseFL; 32% of those were outside Ochiai Top-2.
limits: Wrong-output bugs are the hard class, as SemLoc also finds.
agent_relevance: Our S5 should expect output-error cases to need value-level evidence.

source: Wu et al. (2023) Large Language Models in Fault Localisation
finding: ChatGPT-3.5 and 4 on Defects4J versus SBFL, MBFL, SmartFL. Adding the failing-test error log improves accuracy and consistency.
numbers: ChatGPT-4 with log: mean Top-1 of 23.13, 46.9% above SmartFL at function level. At class level GPT-4 is 49.9% lower than SmartFL. 44 faults (23.66%) localised by GPT-4 (Log) but not by SmartFL on average.
limits: Context length hurts: class-level code collapses performance. Results vary run to run (consistency checked).
agent_relevance: Short context plus error log wins; long context loses to coverage-based tools.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) AutoCodeRover: Autonomous Program Improvement
finding: An LLM agent uses AST code search; optional SBFL from tests gives hint methods to the search.
numbers: SWE-bench lite (300 tasks): resolved 57 without SBFL, 66 with SBFL (19.0% to 22.0%). ACR-sbfl uniquely resolves 7 instances not resolved in the other runs.
limits: SBFL needs a test suite; gain depends on its quality. Cost 40k tokens ($0.47) per task for the SBFL variant.
agent_relevance: Working example of SBFL used inside an LLM agent loop: a hint list, not a final answer. Gain: 3 points.

source: Zhong, Wang, Shang (2024) LDB: Debug like a Human
finding: Segments programs into basic blocks and shows intermediate variable values from execution to the LLM, which checks each block.
numbers: Improves baseline pass rate by up to 9.8% on HumanEval, MBPP and TransCoder.
limits: Not spectrum-based; value-level trace. Abstract read.
agent_relevance: A value-level alternative to coverage, matches SemLoc finding that values matter.

source: Pearson et al. (2017) Evaluating and improving fault localization (ICSE)
finding: Replicated 10 literature claims comparing SBFL and MBFL techniques. On artificial faults 7 claims hold as significant; on real faults every previous result is refuted or insignificant.
numbers: 2995 artificial faults, 310 real faults, 6 Java programs. Only 3 of 7 significant artificial-fault claims had non-negligible effect size. About 40% of past results reversed on real faults (e.g. Metallaxis beats Ochiai on mutants, Ochiai beats Metallaxis on real faults). DStar vs Tarantula: no significant difference on real faults.
limits: Java only (Defects4J). Techniques: Ochiai, Tarantula, DStar, Barinel, Op2, Metallaxis, MUSE.
agent_relevance: Benchmarks of mutants overstate SBFL formula differences. Do not tune on seeded faults.

source: Pearson et al. (2017) Top-N rates on real faults
finding: Share of real faults with the defect in the top 5, 10 or 200 of the ranking.
numbers: 395 real faults. Best-case: hybrid MCBFL 36% (Top-5), 45% (Top-10); DStar 30%, 39%; Metallaxis 29%, 39%. Average case: DStar 18% Top-5, 26% Top-10; hybrid 23%, 31%. Worst case: DStar 17%, 23%. Cited: 98% of practitioners want the defect in the top 10.
limits: Hybrid beats others but not practically significantly on EXAM score.
agent_relevance: Roughly 1 in 4 real faults are inside SBFL top 10 in the average case; a rank list alone is a weak scaffold.

source: Abreu, Zoeteweij, van Gemund (2007) On the Accuracy of Spectrum-based Fault Localization
finding: Introduced the Ochiai similarity coefficient for program spectra and argued it ranks faulty components better than Tarantula and Jaccard on the Siemens set.
numbers: Exact percentages not verified this session.
limits: Not opened. Cited as reference [1] inside AutoFL and FuseFL texts that were read.
agent_relevance: Founding paper for the Ochiai score used in every LLM hybrid above.

source: Parnin, Orso (2011) Are automated debugging techniques actually helping programmers?
finding: Human study of ranked-list debugging aids; cited in the FuseFL reference list. Reported little practical help for programmers.
numbers: Details not verified this session.
limits: Not opened. Only the citation was seen.
agent_relevance: Human use of rank lists is weaker than rank metrics suggest; explanations may matter more (see AutoFL developer study).

source: Jones, Harrold (2005) Empirical evaluation of the Tarantula automatic fault-localization technique
finding: Origin of Tarantula, colour-ranking of statements by pass/fail coverage.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Not opened. Tarantula is a baseline in FuseFL, SemLoc and Pearson, which were read.
agent_relevance: Tarantula is the weakest SBFL baseline in FuseFL Top-1 (89).
